nv_rise_and_shine.blurb: Rise and Shine is a small limestone wall tucked on the west side of Mount Potosi, set opposite the main cliffs of Sleepy Hollow. It holds ten sport routes that start at 5.8 and run up past 5.13, with the weight in the 5.12s and a gentle pair of moderates to open with. The face looks to the southeast, so it catches sun for most of the day, which makes it a natural pick for cooler months, while the neighbouring walls stay shadier. The rock is steep and featured, with a cave and tufa-style features showing up in photos. A short cairned path leads up from the Sleepy Hollow parking area.

nv_yeti_cave.blurb: Yeti Cave is a compact bouldering cave high on Mount Charleston in the Spring Mountains, part of the limestone bouldering found around Kyle Canyon. It holds ten problems, all hard: the lowest is V5, most sit around V8, and a few reach V10 and V11, with plenty of linkups possible between lines. A social trail climbs uphill from a roadside gravel pullout and reaches the cave in about five minutes. At roughly 8,000 feet it suits warmer months better than winter, and the local limestone tends to be abrasive on the skin. Crowds are modest compared with the main boulders at The Subway.

nv_hinkey_summit.blurb: Hinkey Summit is a single rocky wall at the top of the pass at the north end of Paradise Valley, in the Santa Rosa Range. Its ten climbs mix single-pitch sport lines with a few longer multi-pitch routes, ranging from 5.6 up to 5.11, so there is something for a moderate party as well as a few tougher leads. The wall faces mostly west and southwest, with a large arch on its north side and a shallow cave in the middle. It is the highest crag in the valley, so it tends to run cooler and breezier than the lower walls, and the gravel road up can hold snow into early spring.

nv_rodeo_wall.blurb: Rodeo Wall is a south-facing limestone cliff in the La Madre area, just west of Las Vegas. It carries ten sport routes, mostly 5.10 with a few 5.11s and a single 5.12, and the lines are varied with unusual features and plenty of fossils in the rock. Sun hits the face and the ridge blocks the north wind, so it is warm on a winter day. Reaching it takes a long, mostly flat walk along a wash followed by a steep final pitch on a faint, cairned path, so the crowds stay thin. Rock quality is decent, though limestone here can be sharp.

nv_cobre.blurb: Cobre is a big pyramid-shaped rock in the Toano Range of eastern Nevada, visible from the interstate west of Wendover and sometimes labelled Sam's Rock on maps. Most of its ten climbs are multi-pitch trad lines, with a few sport routes thrown in, and grades run from 5.6 into the 5.10s, with a single 5.11. Moderate routes of four and five pitches are the highlights, and faces point in all four directions, so you can chase sun or shade. The drive in uses dirt roads off the highway; a high-clearance vehicle helps but four-wheel drive is not needed. Expect a quiet, remote outing.

nv_california_crag.blurb: California Crag is a small sandstone alcove in the Calico Hills of Red Rock, reached off the trail from the Sandstone Quarry lot. Nine of its ten routes are bolted sport lines, and there is one trad route. Grades start at 5.10, concentrate in the 5.11s, and climb to a few 5.12s and one 5.13, so it suits climbers warming up toward harder projects rather than beginners. The alcove is sheltered from wind and gets afternoon sun, which makes it a popular winter choice. The walk in is short, around five minutes, up a water-streaked slope to the base.
